correctness.rationale: An atomic formula over named zero and multiplication can depend only on the zero flags and equality partition of the up-to-six matrix endpoints of three assigned variables. Upon one replacement at most four endpoint labels remain and at most two new labels are needed, yielding a permanent Duplicator strategy for every pair of index sizes at least six. The exhaustive orbit quotient includes all 255 possible equality patterns, all existing patterns for each index size, and every possible one-variable replacement; recursive rank colors characterize every counting-free FO^3 formula by structural induction. Independently written concrete triple enumeration through index six reproduces the complete rank-color partition 1,2,3,5,6 at quantifier ranks 0,...,4, with stabilization after four. Finite enumeration proves exactly the five small-index separations; the uniform back-and-forth argument proves the infinite tail.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete, infinite-family finite-variable classification of the combinatorial Brandt inverse semigroups, including the first unbounded-depth point where earlier rank-three equivalence breaks: rank four separates indices five and six, yet no later rank distinguishes any two indices at least six. It determines six theories, their sharp minimum family representatives and exact rank spectrum. The two-endpoint structure of matrix units, not arbitrary parameter slicing, explains why the smallest stable index is six, corresponding to 37 semigroup elements.
